summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would prevent the parliamentary broadcasting committee from imposing conditions that ban the use of footage of parliamentary proceedings for satire or ridicule.
It would add a specific limit to the committee’s existing power to set rebroadcasting conditions, allowing parliamentary excerpts to be used for those purposes.
The change would start the day after Royal Assent, while general requirements about context, fairness and accuracy could still apply to all rebroadcasts.
changes: Committee conditions could no longer prohibit satirical rebroadcasts of parliamentary proceedings.
The same restriction would apply to conditions banning footage used for ridicule.
The new limit would take effect the day after Royal Assent.
summary.affected: The Joint Committee on the Broadcasting of Parliamentary Proceedings and people rebroadcasting parliamentary footage for satire or ridicule are affected.

speeches.speaker: Nick Xenophon
speeches.brief: The Parliamentary Proceedings Broadcasting Amendment Bill 2013 was introduced to amend the Parliamentary Proceedings Broadcasting Act 1946, and the bill was read a first time.
